started. See [ADR-0819](adr/0819-graph-integrity-eval.md).

The vector/FTS extensions that opening needs are loaded the way the service loads them (a staged
bundle, or lbug's own install into your home directory). They are never written into the workspace.

## The mapping file

The mapping is data, kept next to the fixture (`crates/eval/fixtures/retrieval-v2/graph-mapping.json`),
so a second corpus or a different relation vocabulary needs no code change.

```json
{
  "mapping_version": 1,
  "kinds": { "project": { "node_types": ["Project"] }, "vendor": { "node_types": ["Vendor", "Organization"] } },
  "links": {
    "Owner": { "relation_types": [
      { "name": "OWNED_BY", "direction": "subject_to_object" },
      { "name": "OWNS",     "direction": "object_to_subject" } ] }
  },
  "junk": { "prefixes": ["recap-", "digest-"] }
}
```

- `kinds`: skeleton entity `kind` → the node type labels accepted for it.
- `links`: skeleton fact attribute → the accepted relation types. `direction` is stated **relative to
  the skeleton fact's subject** (the fact's `entity`): `subject_to_object` means the edge source is
  the subject and the target is the value entity; `object_to_subject` is the reverse. Direction is
  declared per accepted relation type and is never inferred. Accepting a free-form name
  (`MANAGES`) is how the same format covers graphs built without an ontology.
- `junk.prefixes`: first slug segments that mark a note ID (see [Junk](#junk)).
- A kind in the skeleton with no `kinds` entry, or a link-shaped attribute with no `links` entry, is
  listed in the report as **unmapped** and **excluded** from the relevant denominators; it is not
  counted as a failure.

The report records the SHA-256 of the skeleton and the mapping. `--compare` refuses two reports
whose hashes differ.

## Matching rules

Each rule is defined once, in `crates/eval/src/graph_integrity/rules.rs`.

- **Normalisation.** Lowercase; `_`, `-` and any whitespace read as one space; ends trimmed. So
  `Cedar_Core`, `CEDAR-CORE` and `cedar  core` are the same name, and `OWNED_BY` equals `owned by`.
- **Name match.** Equality of normalised names. Never a substring, never an alias, never fuzzy:
  `Cedar Core` does not match `Cedar Supply` or `Cedar`.
- **Node of an entity.** Every node whose normalised name equals the entity's. Several nodes means
  the entity is *split*; edges on any of them count as incident to the entity.
- **Type match.** Some entry of the node's `labels` (the type plus its ancestors) equals,
  case-insensitively, one of the mapping's `node_types` for the kind. The implicit `Entity` label
  never counts. `labels` is used rather than `kind`, which is an identity field that is `Entity`
  unless the ontology marks the type identity-bearing.
- **Edge type.** The stored `relation_type` when non-empty, else the edge `name`, compared through
  normalisation against the mapping's `name`s.
- **Value text.** The normalised value must occur in the normalised edge `fact` at alphanumeric word
  boundaries (so `6` does not match inside `96`). This is an exact-string rule: a fact restated
  as `4200` for `$4,200` is "not stated" although the value is present. **"Not stated" therefore
  over-counts the true misses (it is an upper bound on them) and "stated" under-counts, so "stated"
  is a lower bound.** The word-boundary containment can push the other way only in rare cases (a short
  value such as `9` found in an unrelated mention on an incident edge), so neither figure is exact.

## Metrics

All counts are reported as numerator/denominator where a denominator is meaningful, identically in
`report.md` and `report.json`.

### Typing

- **Found**: skeleton entities with at least one matching node, of all skeleton entities.
- **Split**: entities matched by two or more nodes (a count).
- **Typed**: entities, among those whose kind is mapped, with at least one matching node carrying
  an accepted type. An absent entity is not typed. The denominator is the number of mapped entities.

### Links, per attribute and in total

A *true link* is a skeleton fact whose value is itself a skeleton entity and whose attribute has a
`links` entry, de-duplicated by (subject, attribute, value entity). Per link:

- **Present**: any edge, of any type and in either direction, between a node of the subject and a
  node of the value entity.
- **Expected relation type**: among those edges, at least one whose type is accepted for the
  attribute.
- **Direction correct**: among links with the expected type, at least one expected-type edge whose
  orientation matches that relation type's declared `direction`. Judged only among edges of the
  expected type; a link with both a forward and a reversed edge counts as correct. The denominator
  is the number of links with the expected type, so `56/71` reads "56 of the 71 typed links point the
  right way".

### Value facts

A *value fact* is a skeleton fact whose attribute is not a mapped link and whose value is not a
skeleton entity, de-duplicated by (entity, attribute, value). The denominator is all of them.

- **Stated**: some edge incident to a node of the entity has the value in its `fact` text.
- **Misattached**: some such edge that states the value has, as its other endpoint, a node that is a
  *different* skeleton entity, and its `fact` text does not name that entity. For example
  "Marlin Core has a monthly budget of $4,200" stored as `Marlin Core HAS_MEASURE Tomas Kowalski`.
  An edge whose text does name the other entity (a person set the budget) is a legitimate relation,
  not misattached. The two flags are independent: that Marlin Core edge is both stated and
  misattached; each fact is counted once per flag.

A self-loop on the entity (the representation of a literal-valued fact under an ontology since
#823, see [ontology.md](ontology.md#literal-valued-facts)) that states the value counts as stated
and is never misattached, since its other end is the entity itself.

**Why a fact is not stated (`--unstated-breakdown`, #823).** "Stated" reads only edge `fact` text,
so a value can be in the graph and still count as not stated. With the flag, each not-stated value
fact is put in the first of these that holds:

1. **Only in the entity's node summary**: the value (exact bounded match, as for "stated") is in a
   `summary` of one of the entity's own nodes.
2. **On another entity**: the value is on an edge *not* incident to the entity, or in another node's
   name or summary. For example "The offsite will take place in Aarhus" on an `offsite` node's edge.
3. **Present in another surface form**: an incident edge or the entity's own summary states it in a
   form the exact match misses. A `[day] Month YYYY` value matches its ISO (`2027-03`, `2026-11-02`)
   and abbreviated (`Mar 2027`) spellings; any other value with digits matches when all its number
   tokens appear, separators removed (`$4,200` ≈ `4200 USD`, `98.5%` ≈ `98.5 percent`). This is
   loose, since a small number can match an unrelated figure, so this group is an upper bound.
4. **Absent**: none of the above.

The breakdown is diagnostic and does not change the stated or misattached definitions.

### Junk

Nodes **named like a note ID**. A node is junk when it is not a skeleton entity and either its
normalised name equals a normalised note ID from the skeleton (`project-cedar-core-1`), or its raw
name is lowercase slug-shaped (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)+`), starts with one of `junk.prefixes` and has
an all-digit segment (`recap-01-aiko-osei`, `digest-047`). A node that merely looks unusual is not
junk. This is measured here and fixed elsewhere.

### Signature

- **Marks**: the number of edges carrying a stored `signature_mismatch` mark (#816), per edge type,
  read from the edge `attributes` JSON key `signature_mismatch` (null or `false` do not count; the
  key name is the constant `SIGNATURE_MARK_KEY`). When **no** edge carries the key, the report says
  marks are *absent* (a graph or build without #816) so that zero is not read as "clean".
- **Fit / reversed / neither**, per edge type, against the ontology's declared signature
  (`source_type` → `target_type`, each a name or a list since #816): *fit* when the source node's
  labels include any of the source types and the target's include any of the target types (labels
  already include ancestors); *reversed* when they satisfy it swapped and do not fit; *neither*
  otherwise. The declared types are resolved as #816's ingest check resolves them (names the
  ontology does not declare are ignored). An empty side matches anything; a relation with no
  endpoint types, and a `symmetric` relation, is counted as *unconstrained*. Edge types in the graph
  that the ontology does not declare are listed separately. With no ontology, or an ontology with no
  signatures, the section is reported as not applicable.

## Comparing two graphs

`--compare <report.json>` prints, for every metric, the earlier value, this run's value, the signed
delta (`this − earlier`) and whether it is an improvement (higher is better for found, typed, links
and stated; lower is better for split, misattached, junk, marks, reversed and neither). `run_meta`
(workspace path, version, timestamp) is ignored. For ratio metrics the verdict is judged by the
rate (`num/den`), not the numerator, because the denominator can differ between graphs (for example
direction-correct is `35/35` on a free-form graph and `56/71` under an ontology: the delta is `+21`
but the verdict is "worse rate"); such rows are marked "(denominators differ)". A different skeleton
or mapping hash exits 2, but `report.md` and `report.json` are still written to `--out` first; a file
that is not a valid report exits 1 naming the file.

## Determinism

The same workspace, skeleton, mapping and ontology give identical JSON. The only run-dependent data
(workspace path, tool version, timestamp) is in a separate `run_meta` block.

## Reconciliation with the E13 baseline

The E13 table in #819 came from a one-off script outside LCG that is not in this repository.

> **Provenance of the figures below.** The numbers in this section are **maintainer-reported**: the
> maintainer ran the command on three kept v2 workspaces (free-form, ontology v3.1, v3.1 after the
> #816 repair) and reported the results on PR #822, including that the workspaces were byte-identical
> afterwards and that a run takes about 0.14 s. The kept workspaces and the E13 script are not in
> this repository, so these figures cannot be reproduced from the repo alone, and SC-001 is not
> verified by anything committed here. The repo's own checks are the unit tests (including the
> hand-built graph and the shipped-mapping coverage test).

**Denominators.** The command finds **60** true links (five attributes × 12 pairs) and **440**
literal value facts; E13 used 72 and 428 (the same sum of 500). The difference is the 12 `Location`
links: E13 scored them as links because the value resolves to a graph node, while here a skeleton
fact is a link only when its value is a skeleton entity, so `Location` counts as a value fact. Excluding
`Location` from E13's figures gives this command's link rows:

| | expected relation type | direction correct |
|---|---|---|
| ontology v3.1 | 59/60 | **44/59** (Account manager 6/12, Exception approver 5/12) |
| v3.1 after #816 repair | 59/60 | **59/59** |
| free-form | 53/60 | 53/53 |

As reported, these equal E13's 56/71 → 44/59 and 71/71 → 59/59 once its 12 `Location` links are removed. Scoring
`Location` as a link (`LOCATED_IN`, subject to object, when its value resolves to a graph node, as E13
did) is a possible later extension of the mapping and the scoring rule.

**Other rows (maintainer-reported).** Typing is 47/48 on the ontology graphs with all 48 entities found; junk nodes are 13
on the ontology graphs (the same list as E13); value facts are 293/440 stated with 27 misattached,
against E13's 290/428 and 29 under its looser matching; all 975 `signature_mismatch` marks written by
the #816 repair are read on the repaired workspace.

**The mapping must name the ontology's relation types.** A link attribute whose mapping lists only
free-form names scores 0/12 expected type and 0/0 direction on an ontology graph, which hides the
defect the report exists to catch. This happened for `Account manager` (`CONTACT_FOR`) and
`Exception approver` (`APPROVES`) until they were added. The unit test
`shipped_v2_mapping_covers_the_ontology_relation_types` requires every v2 ontology relation type
(`OWNS`, `SUPPLIED_BY`, `CONTACT_FOR`, `APPROVES`, `REPORTS_TO`) to be in the mapping with the
expected direction. A mapping for another corpus needs the same check against its ontology.

Remaining residuals come from the string rules above: the junk count depends on the note-ID rule (an
exact ID or a prefixed slug with a digit segment), and free-form typing depends on the `node_types`
list in the mapping, which is the tuning point for a free-form graph's labels.

## Value-fact misattachment (#823)

Under an ontology, value facts were pinned to unrelated entities (27 of 440 misattached on the
ontology v3.1 graph above, against 2 free-form). #823 stores a literal-valued fact as a self-loop on
the entity it describes ([ADR-0823](adr/0823-literal-object-edges-as-self-loops.md)). The acceptance
targets: misattached at most 3 under ontology v3.1, stated not lower than the baseline, and the other
metrics within ±1 of a baseline from the same commit (direction-correct compared as a rate when the
denominators differ), with free-form unchanged within ±1.

### Why value facts are not stated: free-form proxy

> **Provenance.** Research for #823 analysed the checked-in free-form v2 cassette
> (`crates/eval/fixtures/retrieval-v2/cassette.jsonl`, recorded 2026-11-18 with Haiku 4.5, from
> prompts that predate #816 and #824) with a script kept outside the repository. It counts the
> *union of extractions* across the cassette's 1,006 calls, not a stored graph, so its figures
> approximate the command's rather than reproduce them (252/440 stated, against E13's free-form
> 259/428; 2 misattached, matching E13). The ontology v3.1 graph is not in the
> repository; its breakdown comes from `--unstated-breakdown` on the maintainer's kept workspace
> (below).

Of the 440 value facts, 201 were not stated on any edge of their entity in the stating note:

| Cause | Facts |
|---|---|
| Only in the entity's node summary | **138** |
| On another entity: an edge not incident to it | 23 |
| On another entity: another node's name or summary | 13 |
| Present in another surface form | 3 |
| Absent | 24 |

Most of the gap is not missing data: two thirds of it sits in the entity's summary, which "stated"
does not read. Only about 24 facts (5%) look genuinely absent, so a follow-up fix for the gap is
warranted only if the ontology graph's breakdown differs materially. 335 of the 1,006 chunks had
fewer than two entities, which the free-form prompt gives no way to carry an edge for.

### Before and after (maintainer-reported, pending)

> **Provenance.** To be filled in from the figures the maintainer reports on the #823 PR. Like
> #819's, these runs need kept v2 workspaces and live extraction, which the repository alone cannot
> reproduce. The repository's own checks are the deterministic tests (`crates/core/tests/literal_object_edges.rs`,
> the prompt golden file, and the graph-integrity unit tests).

Produce each arm from a fresh extraction with the same model and settings. **Before** is `main` at
the merge base without this change, **after** is this branch. Ontology-mode ingest uses
`lcg-eval retrieval --ontology` and kept workspaces (#821, ADR-0821), now on `main`:

```sh
# per arm and mode: extract v2 into a kept workspace, then
target/release/lcg-eval graph-integrity --workspace <ws-before> --unstated-breakdown --out <dir-before>
target/release/lcg-eval graph-integrity --workspace <ws-after>  --unstated-breakdown --out <dir-after> \
  --compare <dir-before>/report.json
```

Also read a sample of the after-change `HAS_MEASURE`, `HAS_TERM` and `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges: a pin
moved into a compound fact that names the other entity passes the metric while staying wrong.

## Not covered

Repairing misattached or missing value facts in stored graphs (#823 prevents new misattachments at
ingest but does not repair existing graphs), fixing note-ID junk nodes, running this in CI on every
PR (it needs a kept workspace), and corpora without a skeleton.

# Retrieval experiments: master record

Source: https://docs.liminis.app/liminis-context-graph/retrieval-experiments


This is the record of every retrieval experiment and its result: what was tried, what it scored, and what was decided. Add a new entry for every eval run that informs a decision, including the ones that fail.

**Goal:** LCG retrieval should beat qmd for the Liminis Notes agent.

## Standard setup (unless an entry says otherwise)

- **Harness:** `lcg-eval retrieval --k 10 --embedding-profile bge-v1.5 --replay-cassette … --embedder-uds …`
  - Extraction is replayed from a committed Haiku 4.5 cassette, so ingest is deterministic.
  - Runs with `--no-grounded` use label-based nDCG and need no judge.
  - Judged runs use a Sonnet 4.6 judge with a judge cache.
- **Embedder:** BGE base v1.5, Core ML, in the LocalInference sidecar.
- **Corpora:**
  - **v2:** `meridian-notebook-2` / `meridian-questions-3`. 408 notes and 244 questions, of which 210 are scored.
    - Categories: direct, paraphrase, temporal, answer, multi-hop and passage, plus negatives.
    - **Tune on v2 only.**
  - **v1:** `fernhill-notebook-1`. 31 notes and 40 scored questions.
    - Categories: direct, paraphrase, temporal and answer. Direct questions are near the ceiling.
    - **v1 is the holdout:** report it for final settings and never tune on it.
- **Metric:** nDCG@10, with paired-bootstrap 95% intervals. Treat a difference as real only when its interval excludes 0.
- **Artifacts:** each run's `report.md` / `report.json` is kept by the maintainer, outside the repo. The PR or issue comment linked in each entry has the full tables.
- **Methodology:** see [Retrieval-Quality Evaluation](retrieval-quality-evaluation.md) for the harness, corpora and question format.
- **Graph-QA results** (E13 and later) come from `lcg-eval graph-qa` and nothing else ([#821](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/821)). There are two steps:
  1. Ingest v2 with `retrieval --ontology crates/eval/fixtures/retrieval-v2/ontology-v3.1.yaml --keep-workspace <ws>`.
  2. Run `graph-qa --workspace <ws> --plans crates/eval/fixtures/retrieval-v2/e13-v5-plans.json` over the committed `graph-questions.jsonl`.

  Report `route` on E13 (all 129 questions) and on E13/test. Graph-QA uses answer accuracy, not nDCG. See [Standard setup for graph-QA results](retrieval-quality-evaluation.md#standard-setup-for-graph-qa-results).

## Current standing (2026-11-20, main after [#806](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/806), [#796](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/796) and [#802](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/802))

| v2 nDCG@10 | overall | direct | paraphrase | temporal | answer | multi-hop | passage | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qmd | 0.507 | 0.639 | 0.347 | 0.529 | 0.700 | 0.473 | 0.353 | 1.8 s |
| qmd-rerank | 0.476 | 0.623 | **0.475** | 0.335 | 0.573 | 0.430 | 0.422 | 3.5 s |
| `lcg-passages-raw` (pre-[#806](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/806) default) | 0.574 | 0.768 | 0.281 | 0.619 | 0.779 | 0.673 | 0.343 | 24 ms |
| `lcg-passages` (default, belief-aware) | 0.653 | 0.826 | 0.328 | 0.745 | 0.918 | 0.758 | 0.361 | 25 ms |
| **`lcg-passages-belief-rerank`** (opt-in) | **0.759** | 0.910 | 0.328 | **0.800** | **0.942** | 0.740 | **0.913** | 1.9 s |

- **v1:** the default scores 0.894 and belief plus rerank 0.935. The qmd row on v1 (0.834 / 0.836) is from the Ollama-embedder era, so it doesn't compare directly.
- **Per-question oracle on v2:** 0.814. The remaining gap is mostly **paraphrase**, where qmd-rerank still leads (0.475 against 0.328).

## Experiments

Newest first. **Δ** is against the stated baseline, paired on v2 unless marked.

### E15: score separation and lexical-leg semantics ([#863](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/863), probe on branch `fabrik/issue-863` @ `e9d5177f`, v2, 2026-11-21). Measured, no product change

The question (from [#848](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/848)): is [#812](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/812)'s absolute `min_score` floor (default 0.5) safe in hybrid mode? Related: does the lexical leg match any term or all terms ([#843](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/843))?

- **Method:**
  - `lcg-eval retrieval-score-probe` (eval-only) sends `knowledge_search_passages` with `min_score = 0` in `vector`, `hybrid` and `hybrid-belief` modes, then again with `min_score = 0.5`. It records the top-10 `score` and `similarity` per query.
  - Service `0.19.1`, BGE-base v1.5 Core ML, profile `bge-v1.5`, k = 10, all 408 notes ingested through a stub extractor that extracts nothing (the committed free-form cassette no longer replays on this branch; passage search reads only Episodic nodes).
  - Three query sets: **answerable** (140: direct, paraphrase, answer, passage), **hard negatives** (the 34 `negative` questions) and **off-topic** (34 constructed queries in `offtopic-queries.jsonl`: 16 unrelated-domain, 8 gibberish, 10 common-words-only).
  - The FTS question was checked by running `QUERY_FTS_INDEX` through raw Cypher on the ingested corpus, with and without `conjunctive := true`.
- **Top-1 vector cosine** (hybrid's best vector cosine is within 0.003):

| set | n | min | p10 | median | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| answerable | 140 | 0.475 | 0.554 | 0.668 | 0.790 | 0.867 |
| hard-negative | 34 | 0.582 | 0.616 | 0.690 | 0.732 | 0.764 |
| off-topic | 34 | 0.407 | 0.429 | 0.469 | 0.567 | 0.601 |

- **Separation from the answerable set (AUC):** off-topic 0.961, hard negatives 0.441 (cosine); fused hybrid score 0.947 and 0.410. Fused hybrid `score` saturates at 1.4/60 = 0.0233 (answerable median 0.0230, off-topic median 0.0167), a rank-only value.
- **Under the 0.5 floor:**

| | vector | hybrid |
|---|---|---|
| answerable queries returning a top-1 | 139/140 | 140/140 |
| hard-negative queries returning hits | 34/34 | 34/34 |
| off-topic queries returning hits | 13/34 | 25/34 |
| lexical-only hits on off-topic queries | n/a | 115 |

  - Hybrid's extra hits are BM25 matches for unrelated-domain queries, tagged `similarity == null` with a fused score of about 0.0067. On answerable queries, the 140 lexical-only hits that survive the floor contain 6 relevant notes (4%); the 1,260 vector-backed hits contain 139 (11%).
  - The best single cosine threshold is 0.548 (keeps 91.4% of answerable, admits 11.8% of off-topic). No threshold separates the hard negatives.
- **FTS leg:** `cedar` 34 matches; `zzqxvk` 0; `cedar zzqxvk` **34** by default and **0** with `conjunctive := true`. The shipped leg is any-term (OR). No E3 variant changed this.
- **Mergers (for [#849](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/849)):** a name-only pair scan of the E13 graphs found 0 of 48 skeleton entities merged (free-form and ontology v3.1), 0 names on more than one node, 8 and 28 distinct node pairs at name cosine ≥ 0.85, and 13 and 17 exact-duplicate edge groups (by design: ingest does not deduplicate edges).
- **Learned:**
  - The 0.5 floor is **safe** on v2 with this embedder (99.3% of answerable top-1s kept) but is **not an abstention mechanism**, and it is weaker in hybrid mode than in vector mode because the BM25 leg is never floored.
  - Hybrid's fused `score` is not a relevance and no floor on it is meaningful; `similarity` is the relevance signal.
  - The margin is thin: the lowest answerable top-1 is 0.475 and the 10th percentile 0.554. The 0.5 default came from a different embedder run ([#811](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/811)), so it needs remeasuring per embedder.
  - Near-domain negatives score above the answerable median in every mode.
  - Limits: synthetic corpus, 34 hand-written off-topic queries, one embedder, rerank leg not measured.
- **Decision:** no default changes. Follow-ups are recommended in [`docs/research/webbrain-retrieval-suggestions.md`](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/blob/main/docs/research/webbrain-retrieval-suggestions.md): a work issue for per-leg evidence on hybrid passages (#848), a probe (E16) of an all-terms and a "BM25 must agree" lexical leg (#843), declining #849, and a work issue for `lcg-eval retrieval` input digests and `--compare` (#847).

### E14: LLM note summaries as extra retrieval units (offline probe, main @ `86f135dc` service, v2, 2026-11-21). Promising for paraphrase, borderline overall

The question: does an LLM-written summary per note, indexed beside the raw passages, close the paraphrase gap (0.328 against qmd-rerank's 0.475)? The idea comes from a review of WebBrain's retrieval design ([#843](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/843)–[#849](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/849) are the related suggestions). This is an offline probe with no LCG change.

- **Method:**
  - Haiku 4.5 wrote one summary per note (408 calls): 3–6 plain sentences plus one key-concepts sentence, no headings. BGE embeds them.
  - The baseline (a) is shipped `knowledge_search_passages` top 10 with `belief_aware` and rerank, on a copy of the free-form v2 workspace. It reproduces the record: 0.758 against 0.759, and the default 0.653 against 0.653.
  - Note-level nDCG@10 by `lcg-eval`'s rules.
  - The mxbai rerank sidecar scored the summaries.

| v2 nDCG@10 | overall | direct | paraphrase | temporal | answer | multi-hop | passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) passages, belief + rerank | 0.758 | 0.910 | 0.328 | 0.800 | 0.935 | 0.740 | 0.913 |
| (b) summaries only, dense | 0.540 | 0.716 | 0.346 | 0.580 | 0.747 | 0.621 | 0.223 |
| (c) RRF(a, b) | 0.677 | 0.855 | 0.366 | 0.707 | 0.878 | 0.721 | 0.568 |
| (d0) a's passages re-scored by mxbai alone (control) | 0.710 | 0.863 | 0.397 | 0.716 | 0.784 | 0.596 | 0.954 |
| (d) mxbai over a's passages + top-10 summaries | 0.731 | 0.862 | **0.526** | 0.682 | 0.784 | 0.616 | 0.954 |
| (d2) a's order, summary notes inserted by rerank score | **0.771** | 0.914 | 0.412 | 0.800 | 0.935 | 0.717 | 0.913 |

- **Result:**
  - **RRF fusion loses.** (c) is −0.081 [−0.109, −0.054] overall and −0.093 on temporal. Summaries carry no supersession signal, so (b) is −0.22 on temporal.
  - **Summaries as rerank candidates help paraphrase.** (d) against its own control (d0) is +0.129 [+0.029, +0.233] on paraphrase, +0.021 [−0.005, +0.047] overall, and −0.034 [−0.101, +0.033] on temporal. Its paraphrase score of 0.526 is above qmd-rerank's 0.475.
  - **Kept inside LCG's belief-aware order (d2):**
    - Overall +0.014 [−0.003, +0.033].
    - Paraphrase +0.084 [+0.002, +0.181]. That's 7 wins and 6 losses of 40, so it's fragile.
    - Temporal unchanged.
    - Multi-hop −0.023 [−0.046, −0.003], because summary notes push passages out of the top 10.
- **Learned:**
  - Re-scoring LCG's passages with the raw reranker alone (d0) loses 0.048 overall against the shipped ranking, so LCG's belief blend is worth about 0.05.
  - The (d2) merge is crude. A proper version puts summary units into LCG's own candidate pool before the belief-aware rerank.
  - There's no dev/test split for these questions, so this is tuned on v2.
- **Decision:** it meets the bar only at the margin, through (d2) on paraphrase. That's worth an implementation probe in LCG: summary passages as rerank candidates inside `knowledge_search_passages`, with belief-aware ordering, and a citation mapped back to the source passage. Not filed yet.

### E13: graph multi-hop probes and an ontology ([#815](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/815), local probe on main @ `19759906`, v2). Promising, not shipped

The question: does the graph answer what chunk search can't (chains, joins, inverse lookups), and does an ontology make it usable?

- **Free-form graph audit (v2, standard cassette):**
  - 2,016 edges carry 1,223 distinct relation types.
  - Hub entities have 80–115 edges.
  - The facts for the 15 real chain questions are present: 15/15 entities resolve and hop 1 is there for 15/15, hop 2 for 12/15.
  - Question-guided walks found the answer in the top fact for at most 7/15, against 1/15 for flat fact search.
  - `knowledge_canonicalize_relations` typed only 26–28% of edges lexically.
- **Ontology v3 → v3.1.** It was written from a purpose statement and 25+4 competency questions (CQs), not from the corpus. Fit was judged by blind classifier agents given only the purpose and the type menu.
  - Bar: ≥ 85% of purpose-relevant ("core") facts typed on both corpora, and κ ≥ 0.8.
  - v3: 93–98% core typed on v2, κ 0.87, but only **45% on v1**. Missing: roles and titles, plans and schedules, proposals, replacement.
  - v3.1 (+`HAS_ROLE`, `SCHEDULED_FOR`, `PROPOSED`, wider `SUPERSEDES`; 27 types): **97% / 97%** on a fresh v2 sample and **98%** on v1, κ 0.82, with incidental typing at 17–24%. The v1 figure is optimistic, since those facts were read while revising.
- **Live re-extraction of v2 under v3.1 (strict), Haiku 4.5 via subscription:**
  - 3,675 calls with 0 errors. The new cassette is `v2-haiku45-onto31`.
  - Result: 2,612 edges over **28 types**, of which 74 are `UNCLASSIFIED` (3%). Nodes went from 769 to 1,202, so entity splitting needs a look.
  - `lcg-entities-facts` nDCG 0.283 → 0.294 (noise). Passages are unaffected.
- **Graph-native question set:** 129 questions in 13 families, shapes from the CQs and gold from the skeleton.
  - Metric "complete": every hop has a gold note among the returned evidence.
  - Metric "answer": every gold answer appears in the returned facts.
  - Passages are scored strictly: all gold notes in the top 10.
  - The walk is LLM-free: exact-name seed, then at each hop the top 3 edges by cosine (10 for lists and joins). "Typed" filters each hop to its CQ relation types.

| runner (graph) | chain-2 (48) | chain-3 (24) | list (31) | join (14) | history (12) | **all (129)** | answer found |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` top 10 | 9 | 0 | 20 | 0 | **12** | 41 | n/a |
| flat facts top 10 (typed graph) | 5 | 0 | 28 | 0 | 10 | 43 | 50 |
| walk, untyped (free-form) | 17 | 3 | 28 | 12 | 9 | 69 | 93 |
| walk, typed + fallback (free-form) | 18 | 4 | 24 | 4 | 1 | 51 | 97 |
| walk, untyped (typed graph) | 22 | 9 | 26 | 11 | 11 | 79 | 95 |
| **walk, typed (typed graph)** | **35** | **19** | **29** | 12 | 9 | **104** | **119** |

- **Learned:**
  - Chunk search can't do chains or joins: `lcg-passages` gets 0/24 on 3-hop and 0/14 on joins, with complete evidence for 41 of 129 questions.
  - A typed walk over the ontology graph gets complete evidence for 104/129 and finds the answer for 119/129, returning about 6 facts against 10 passages.
  - The ontology is the lever. Typing the free-form graph after the fact doesn't help (51, which falls below the untyped walk's 69). Extracting under the ontology does (104).
  - Passages still win change history (12/12 against 9/12), so route by question type.
- **Caveats:**
  - Step 1's walk plan is oracle and "answer found" is substring presence. Step 2 addresses both.
  - v2 is nearly one-to-one (each supplier serves one project), which understates aggregation.
  - The walk and the `--ontology` hook are local patches, not in the repo.
- **Step 2: answer accuracy with a planner and a reader**. Haiku 4.5 via the subscription is both the planner and the reader, and both are cached.
  - The planner sees only the question and the relation-type menu: no families, no gold. It returns a route (graph or passages), a start entity and typed hops.
  - Every runner's context goes to the same reader.
  - Scoring: first answer matches for single answers, set F1 for lists and joins, exact in-order match for history.

| runner (mean score) | chain-2 | chain-3 | list | join | history | **all** | vs passages (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` top 10 | 0.19 | 0.00 | 0.72 | 0.05 | **1.00** | 0.34 | n/a |
| walk, oracle path (typed graph) | 0.90 | 0.92 | 0.77 | 0.62 | 0.50 | 0.80 | +0.46 [+0.35, +0.57] |
| walk, planned path (typed graph) | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.77 | 0.60 | 0.17 | 0.76 | +0.42 [+0.30, +0.54] |
| **route, planned (typed graph)** | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.77 | 0.60 | **1.00** | **0.84** | **+0.50 [+0.40, +0.60]** |
| route, planned (free-form graph) | 0.71 | 0.62 | 0.92 | 0.55 | 0.83 | 0.74 | +0.40 [+0.29, +0.50] |

  - **Planning costs little.** The planned path comes within 0.04 of the oracle path. All 119 graph starts resolved to a node, and the planner sent 10 of 12 history questions to passages.
  - **The ontology matters for the final answer.** Typed against free-form, route-planned scores +0.10 [+0.02, +0.18] (22 wins, 12 losses); walk-oracle +0.08 [+0.01, +0.15]. The gain is in chains (0.90/0.88 against 0.71/0.62). The free-form graph does better on lists (0.92 against 0.77).
  - **Misses:**
    - Some chain-2 questions return nothing on either path. These are gaps in extraction or data, not in planning.
    - Supplier-contact joins stop at the vendor instead of following on to the project.
    - Owner-city joins pull in non-project entities through `OWNS`, because the walk doesn't check the type of the entity it lands on.
    - A history walk returns partial lists, so passages are the right route for history.
  - **Caveats:**
    - The planner's route rule (attribute or history → passages) was written after the step-1 finding, so the route row is not a blind test.
    - The reader is Haiku.
    - The data is synthetic and nearly one-to-one.
- **Step 3: the qmd and rerank baselines on the same set.** The setup:
  - Same planner, same reader, same scoring as step 2.
  - The mxbai-rerank-large-v1 Core ML model was re-staged; its max logit error against PyTorch is 0.006.
  - qmd runs the way lcg-eval calls it, with and without its own reranker. The reader gets the **whole note** for each qmd hit, which is generous to qmd: about 2.3 KB per hit against about 350 characters per LCG passage.

| runner (mean score) | chain-2 | chain-3 | list | join | history | **all** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qmd` | 0.19 | 0.00 | 0.72 | 0.24 | 0.67 | 0.33 |
| `qmd-rerank` | 0.17 | 0.00 | 0.89 | 0.15 | 0.08 | 0.30 |
| `lcg-passages` | 0.19 | 0.00 | 0.72 | 0.05 | **1.00** | 0.34 |
| `lcg-passages-belief-rerank` | 0.21 | 0.00 | 0.88 | 0.00 | 0.92 | 0.37 |
| **route, planned (typed graph + `lcg-passages`)** | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.77 | 0.60 | **1.00** | **0.84** |
| route, planned (typed graph + belief-rerank) | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.77 | 0.60 | 0.92 | 0.83 |

  - **The best chunk search scores 0.30–0.37 on graph-shaped questions.** None of the four passage or qmd configs answers a 3-hop question (0/24).
  - **Routed LCG beats qmd by a wide margin:** +0.51 [+0.41, +0.61] against `qmd` and +0.53 [+0.43, +0.63] against `qmd-rerank`.
  - **qmd's reranker hurts history** (0.08), because it ignores time. LCG's belief ranking keeps history at 0.92–1.00.
  - **Lists favour the rerankers** (0.88–0.89 against the walk's 0.77), so lists are the next place to look for a planner or walk gain.
- **Step 4: walk and planner fixes, with a held-out half.** The questions were split per family into a dev half (67) and a test half (62), seed 815. Misses were read on the dev half only. Each fix is generic: none names a family or a relation path.
  - **v2:** the planner also names the answer's entity type. The walk doesn't step back to nodes it has visited, keeps the final hop on that type (falling back if none match), and takes one completion hop towards that type when the planned hops end elsewhere. Joins rose (0.60 → 0.73), but history fell, because history values carry mixed types.
  - **v3:** adds a hard per-hop edge direction, skips the type filter for history, and gives the reader each endpoint's entity type. Lists rose (0.77 → 0.90), but joins and value chains fell. **Extracted edge direction is unreliable** (for example `Nimbus Supply → Nimbus Core` for "supplied by"), so a hard filter drops correct edges.
  - **v5 (kept):** the v3 plans, with direction as a small ranking bonus (+0.05 cosine) instead of a filter. Typed reader context and no type filter on history, as in v3.

| runner (mean score) | chain-2 | chain-3 | list | join | history | **all** | dev | **test** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| route, planned (step 2) | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.77 | 0.60 | 1.00 | 0.84 | 0.80 | 0.89 |
| route, planned v4 (v2 plans, typed context, no direction) | 0.92 | 0.88 | 0.94 | 0.86 | 0.92 | 0.91 | 0.89 | 0.92 |
| **route, planned v5** | 0.88 | 0.96 | **0.94** | **0.86** | 1.00 | **0.91** | 0.89 | **0.94** |

  - **v5 against step 2:** +0.075 [+0.027, +0.127] on all 129 questions. On the test half it is +0.052 [-0.016, +0.127], which is positive but not separable at n = 62.
  - **v5 against the baselines:** +0.59 [+0.49, +0.68] against `qmd`, +0.62 against `qmd-rerank` and +0.54 against `lcg-passages-belief-rerank`. On the test half: +0.63, +0.67 and +0.59.
  - **The biggest single gain is telling the reader each fact's entity types.** "Helix Core obtains goods from Tern Supply" was answered as nothing until the reader could see that Helix Core is a project.
  - **Noise:** the embedding disk cache rounds vectors to 6 decimal places, which changed a few cosine ties. Route v2's joins moved 0.73 → 0.70 between identical runs.
- **Why the typed graph has more nodes (769 → 1,202):** it isn't entity splitting.
  - All 48 skeleton entities resolve to exactly one node in both graphs.
  - The growth is the ontology's reified kinds: Policy 253, Decision 191, Topic 207, Meeting 70.
  - Core typing is 47/48 correct; Orbit Supply is labelled Project.
  - There are 13 note-ID junk nodes such as `project-quill-core-1`, against 2 free-form. They likely come from the Document type inviting the note itself.
- **Harness:** the embedder sidecar twice left a request hanging with no reply. `traverse_lib.embed` now has a 60 s timeout, retries, batches of 32 and an on-disk cache.
- **Edge direction ([#816](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/816)).** On known-true links, 48/142 typed edges (34%) are reversed: `APPROVES` 79%, `CONTACT_FOR` 75%, `OWNS` 21%, `SUPPLIED_BY` 12%, and `LOCATED_IN` and `REPORTS_TO` 0%. The extractor orients edges by the sentence's subject.
  - **Causes:**
    - The edge prompt never defines direction.
    - Half signatures are not rendered.
    - Endpoints are never checked against the signature.
    - Aliases can't express an inverse.
  - **Simulated fix:** checking endpoint types against full signatures (test ontology v3.2: type lists, `inverse_aliases`, symmetric `WORKS_WITH`) and swapping on a reversed fit, over the existing graph. Reversed links went from 48/142 to **1/142** without re-extraction.
  - **38% of typed edges fit neither way.** They are mostly incidental facts with loose entity types, so the fix flags them and keeps them.
  - The walk results above don't depend on direction, since direction is only a ranking bonus there.
- **Step 5: the [#816](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/816) repair on the stored graph (PR [#817](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/817) @ `e4ba1191`), 2026-11-21.** `knowledge_canonicalize_relations` was run on a copy of the v3.1 workspace, with the ontology swapped for v3.2.
  - **Repair counts:** 164 edges swapped and 975 marked `signature_mismatch`; none dropped (2,620 edges before and after). The dry run matched the real run. A second run swapped 0.
  - **Reversed known-true links:** 48/142 → **1/142 (0.7%)**: `APPROVES` 22 → 0, `CONTACT_FOR` 18 → 1, `OWNS` 6 → 0, `SUPPLIED_BY` 2 → 0. Results posted on PR [#817](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/817).
  - **The repair also retypes.** Under v3.2's alias cleanup, 467 edges changed relation type (439 of them without a swap). For example, `DISCUSSED` went 242 → 350 and `WORKS_ON` 540 → 466. A swap-only arm applies the 136 swaps on edges whose type didn't change, keeping the v3.1 types.

| runner (mean score) | chain-2 | chain-3 | list | join | history | **all** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 (hard direction), old graph | 0.85 | 0.96 | 0.90 | 0.55 | 1.00 | 0.86 |
| v3, swap-only repair | 0.85 | 0.96 | 0.94 | 0.80 | 1.00 | 0.90 |
| v5 (soft direction), old graph | 0.88 | 0.96 | 0.94 | 0.86 | 1.00 | **0.91** |
| v5, swap-only repair | 0.88 | 0.96 | 0.94 | 0.80 | 1.00 | 0.91 |
| v5, full repair (v3.1 menu) | 0.83 | 0.96 | 0.94 | 0.80 | 1.00 | 0.89 |
| v5, full repair (v3.2 menu) | 0.79 | 0.92 | 0.89 | 0.77 | 1.00 | 0.87 |

  - **Hard direction now works.** On the swap-only graph, v3 gains +0.036 [+0.012, +0.067] over the old graph, which was its whole deficit to v5.
  - **No net gain over v5.** v5 against v5 swap-only: -0.006 [-0.023, +0.005]. The soft bonus had already absorbed most of the reversal damage, and this question set has almost no question whose answer turns on direction (inverse lookups such as "who reports to X").
  - **The v3.2 retyping and menu cost slightly:** full repair with the v3.1 menu is -0.022 [-0.053, +0.002] against v5; with the v3.2 menu, -0.040 [-0.078, -0.010]. The planner and walk were tuned on v3.1 types (dev half), so this is a re-tuning cost, not evidence against v3.2.
  - **Decision:** the typed walk keeps direction as a soft preference by default. It's robust to residual errors and equal to hard direction on a clean graph.
- **Step 6: parity of the shipped `knowledge_walk` ([#820](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/820), PR [#825](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/825) @ `86f135dc`) with the v5 probe, 2026-11-21.** The recorded v5 plans were replayed through `knowledge_walk` (soft direction) on a copy of the v3.1 workspace.
  - **Edges:** 112/118 planned questions return the identical edge-uuid set. The 6 others are exact ties between duplicate edges with the same fact text and endpoints. LCG breaks ties by uuid; the probe used Python set order, which varies with the hash seed (6, 12 and 6 differing edges across three seeds). By fact text and endpoints: **118/118**. Edge scores match the probe's cosine to 4 decimal places.
  - **Reader score** (`route-planned5`, walk context from `facts_text`): **0.916** against the probe's 0.915; test half 0.943 against 0.940.
  - **Read-only:** WAL byte-identical after 118 walks.
- **Graph integrity baseline against the skeleton (no LLM).** Filed as [#819](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/819), `lcg-eval graph-integrity`.

| | free-form | ontology v3.1 | v3.1 + repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| skeleton entities typed correctly | 35/48 | 47/48 | 47/48 |
| true links present (any edge) | 72/72 | 72/72 | 72/72 |
| true links with expected relation type | 35/72 | 71/72 | 71/72 |
| typed true links, direction correct | 35/35 | 56/71 | **71/71** |
| value facts stated on the right entity | 259/428 | 290/428 | 290/428 |
| value facts pinned to an unrelated entity | 2 | 29 (12 with no correct copy) | 29 |
| note-ID junk nodes | 2 | 13 | 13 |

  - **Free-form graphs never reverse,** because the model names the relation as the sentence reads. They just aren't typed: 35/72.
  - **Two new extraction problems:**
    - **Misattached value facts.** "Marlin Core has a monthly budget of $4,200" is stored as `Marlin Core HAS_MEASURE Tomas Kowalski`.
    - **About a third of value facts are not on their entity's edges at all.** The check is an exact string match, so this is a lower bound.
- **Next:**
  - [#816](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/816) / PR [#817](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/817): merged 2026-11-21 as `468f6ba4`.
  - [#819](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/819): `lcg-eval graph-integrity` merged 2026-11-21 as `76c9c077` (PR [#822](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/822)). Value-fact misattachment fix next.
  - [#820](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/820): `knowledge_walk` passes parity (step 6); PR [#825](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/pull/825) waiting to merge.
  - Inverse-direction questions ("who reports to X", "what does Lena own") in the next question set, since v2 can't show a direction gain.
  - A wider held-out test, since n = 62 can't separate +0.05.
  - `lcg-eval --ontology`.
  - A second corpus with fan-out and the CQs v2 can't instantiate (P3, S2, meetings, provenance).

### E12: graph search plus rerank ([#797](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/797), PR [#801](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/801) @ `672c6de3`). Rejected, closed 2026-11-20

| config | v2 | v1 | paraphrase (v2) | temporal (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages-belief-rerank` | **0.757** | **0.935** | 0.328 | 0.793 |
| `lcg-graph-rerank` | 0.745 | 0.890 | 0.235 | 0.789 |
| `lcg-graph-seeds-rerank` | 0.718 | 0.819 | 0.156 | 0.800 |
| `lcg-graph` (no rerank) | 0.664 | 0.867 | 0.214 | 0.806 |

- **Result:** graph plus rerank against passages plus rerank is −0.012 [−0.040, +0.015] on v2, and −0.045 [−0.109, +0.011] on v1. It met no part of the bar.
- **Learned:**
  - The reranker is the lever: about +0.08 on either first stage.
  - Graph candidates add nothing once the candidates are reranked.
  - Seed linking fails on described (paraphrased) entities.
  - Graph does win on direct questions (0.946) and passage lookups (0.951), which is a possible router signal.
- **Decision:** PR closed unmerged and the branch `fabrik/issue-797` kept. Results are on [#797](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/797).

### E11: graph search before rerank ([#797](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/797), PR [#801](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/801) @ `a3a1e155`). Not distinguishable

- **Result:** `lcg-graph` 0.661 against `lcg-passages-belief` 0.653 on v2: −0.008 [−0.033, +0.018]. On v1 it scored 0.863 against 0.894.
- **Oracle:** 0.795, of which `lcg-graph` captures 83%.
- **Decision:** hold until rerank lands (that became E12).

### E10: mxbai reranker shipped ([#796](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/796), PR [#800](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/800) @ `2471ad5d`). Accepted, merged 2026-11-20 as `d3f1477c`

| config | v2 | v1 | temporal (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` (raw then) | 0.574 | 0.829 | 0.619 |
| `lcg-passages-belief` | 0.653 | 0.894 | 0.745 |
| `lcg-passages-rerank` | 0.707 | 0.938 | 0.777 |
| `lcg-passages-belief-rerank` | **0.759** | 0.935 | 0.800 |

- **Result:**
  - Belief plus rerank against belief: +0.106 [+0.073, +0.142] on v2 and +0.041 [+0.007, +0.082] on v1.
  - Against raw: +0.185 on v2.
- **Merge bar:** met except temporal on v2 (0.800 against the 0.85 target). Accepted, since rerank is opt-in and temporal still improves on the default.
- **Shipped defaults:**
  - mxbai-rerank-large-v1, Core ML fp16, GPU;
  - blend 0.30 / 0.20 / 0.10;
  - 50 candidates, which is also the cap;
  - the superseded factor applies to the whole blended score.

### E9: belief-aware passage ranking as the default ([#806](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/806), PR [#807](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/807) @ `723bbb9f`). Accepted, merged 2026-11-19

- **Result:**
  - New default against `lcg-passages-raw`: +0.078 [+0.061, +0.097] on v2 and +0.065 [+0.027, +0.108] on v1.
  - Every category was level or better on both corpora.
  - Latency was unchanged.

### E8: mxbai blend and candidate-count sweep (Core ML in the PR [#800](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/800) sidecar @ `da2c2078`, v2)

| setting | overall | paraphrase | temporal | multi-hop | passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline `lcg-passages` | 0.574 | 0.281 | 0.619 | 0.673 | 0.343 |
| cross-encoder only, N = 25 | 0.688 | 0.255 | **0.932** | 0.543 | 0.846 |
| cross-encoder only, N = 50 | 0.692 | 0.201 | 0.904 | 0.534 | **0.954** |
| blend 0.75 / 0.60 / 0.40, N = 50 | 0.649 | 0.283 | 0.742 | 0.678 | 0.613 |
| blend 0.50 / 0.40 / 0.30, N = 50 | 0.703 | 0.291 | 0.746 | **0.689** | 0.923 |
| **blend 0.30 / 0.20 / 0.10, N = 50** | **0.707** | 0.290 | 0.777 | 0.666 | 0.925 |

- **Learned:**
  - A light rank prior wins.
  - Pure cross-encoder ordering wins temporal and passage but loses multi-hop.
  - N = 100 silently ran at 50, the clamp, which is now a warning.
  - The Core ML scores matched the Python reference exactly (0.688 at N = 25).
- **Performance:**
  - On the Neural Engine, mxbai (DeBERTa-v3) is 15× slower than on the GPU (3.8 s against 0.26 s per batch of 8). The model loads in 3–4 minutes.
  - fp16 needed a −1e4 mask fill, otherwise padded pairs score NaN. The converter patches are in [#796](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/796).

### E7: reranker model probe (full corpus, paraphrase questions, transformers/MPS)

| model | paraphrase top-1 | top-10 | median rank | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BAAI/bge-reranker-base | 4 | 15 | 15 | weak on paraphrase |
| ibm-granite reranker r2 | 5 | 24 | 9.5 | worse on passage |
| **mixedbread mxbai-rerank-large-v1** | **15** | **35** | **2** | chosen (Apache 2.0, DeBERTa-v3, 435M) |

- **Policy:** no Qwen-family models, which excludes mxbai v2 because it is Qwen-based. BGE is the acceptable fallback.

### E6: bge-reranker-base rerank and Foundation Models expansion (PR [#800](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/800) @ `5d3760fb`, v2)

| config | overall | paraphrase | temporal | passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` | 0.574 | 0.281 | 0.619 | 0.343 |
| `lcg-passages-rerank` (bge-reranker-base) | 0.618 | 0.064 | 0.899 | 0.752 |
| `lcg-passages-expand` | 0.545 | 0.213 | 0.563 | 0.374 |
| `lcg-passages-expand-rerank` | 0.626 | 0.047 | 0.899 | 0.797 |

- **Learned:**
  - bge-reranker-base wrecks paraphrase, and the first version ignored the first-stage rank. That led to the position-aware blend steer and to E7.
  - Before a positional fallback was added (`94d5ca05`), Apple Foundation Models omitted its `lex:` / `vec:` / `hyde:` labels on 79% of queries, and expansion at that head scored 0.465.
  - Expansion stays opt-in and unproven.

### E5: caller query variants ([#802](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/802), PR [#805](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/805)). Shipped opt-in, docs only, merged 2026-11-20

| config | v2 overall | paraphrase | multi-hop | passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages-belief` | 0.653 | 0.328 | **0.757** | 0.361 |
| `lcg-passages-belief-variants` (`87c85525`) | 0.664 | **0.357** | 0.695 | 0.479 |
| `lcg-passages-hybrid-belief` | 0.647 | 0.214 | 0.748 | 0.443 |
| `lcg-passages-hybrid-belief-variants` | **0.665** | 0.296 | 0.689 | **0.554** |

- **History:**
  - First cut, `a0c7e95f`: weights of 2 for the primary and 1 for each variant, with no belief. Variants scored 0.522 against a 0.568 baseline, −0.046 [−0.077, −0.016].
  - Rebalanced: a variant budget of 1.0 against the primary's 2.0, belief applied after fusion, and variants run through the request's own pipeline.
- **Result:**
  - Passage lookups improve: +0.117 for vector and +0.112 for hybrid.
  - Hybrid paraphrase improves by +0.082.
  - Multi-hop drops: −0.062 for vector and −0.059 for hybrid.
- **Cause:** the variants (Sonnet 4.6, written from the question only) drop the named entity, and fusion dilutes notes the primary query already ranked well.
- **Decision:** shipped as opt-in, with guidance to keep named entities. Regenerate the fixture variants with that rule and re-measure together with rerank (open).

### E4: graph search, seed gate ([#797](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/797), PR [#801](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/801) @ `d7078ccd` / `e002f128`, v2)

| config | overall | direct | paraphrase | temporal | passage | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` (no instruction) | 0.568 | 0.756 | 0.150 | 0.628 | 0.477 | 25 ms |
| `lcg-graph-seeds` | 0.599 | 0.875 | **0.000** | 0.795 | 0.605 | 39 ms |
| `lcg-graph-expand` | 0.585 | 0.729 | 0.000 | 0.788 | 0.791 | 130 ms |
| `lcg-graph` | 0.648 | 0.861 | 0.078 | **0.834** | 0.613 | 140 ms |

- **Learned:**
  - The seed gate rejected every described entity, so paraphrase scored 0.
  - With the BGE query instruction (`e002f128`), `lcg-graph` reached 0.653, level with belief.
  - Per-category best configs would give an oracle of 0.842, which led to the composite steer (that became E11 and E12).

### E3: hybrid and belief-aware passages ([#789](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/789), PR [#798](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/issues/798), v2). Merged

| config | v2 | v1 | temporal (v2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` | 0.568 | 0.789 | 0.628 |
| `lcg-passages-hybrid` | 0.572 | n/a | 0.630 |
| `lcg-passages-belief` | 0.649 | n/a | 0.802 |
| `lcg-passages-hybrid-belief` | 0.652 | n/a | 0.802 |

- **Result:**
  - Belief against raw: +0.081 [+0.063, +0.100].
  - Temporal: +0.174 [+0.114, +0.238].
  - Hybrid on its own is about level. The early hybrid-RRF / bonus variants scored 0.527–0.531 on v2 and lost paraphrase.
- **Decision:** belief as opt-in, which became the default in E9.

### E2: BGE query instruction (embedding profile `bge-v1.5` against `none`, v2)

- **Result:** it doubles paraphrase for vector search (0.150 → 0.281) and lifts the overall score slightly (0.568 → 0.574), but hurts named-entity passage lookups (0.477 → 0.343).
- **On v1:** 0.828–0.829 against 0.789 with the Ollama embedder.
- **Decision:** `bge-v1.5` is the standard profile. The composite steer asked for both embeddings fused.

### E1: baselines on v2 (corpus v2 built 2026-11-18, judged)

| config | overall | direct | paraphrase | temporal | answer | multi-hop | passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lcg-passages` | 0.568 | 0.756 | 0.150 | 0.628 | 0.789 | 0.662 | 0.477 |
| `lcg-entities-facts` | 0.283 | 0.284 | 0.009 | 0.389 | 0.360 | 0.186 | 0.529 |
| qmd | 0.507 | 0.639 | 0.347 | 0.529 | 0.700 | 0.473 | 0.353 |
| qmd-rerank | 0.476 | 0.623 | 0.475 | 0.335 | 0.573 | 0.430 | 0.422 |

- **Learned:**
  - v1 is too easy to separate systems: qmd scored 0.834 and LCG passages 0.789 with the Ollama embedder.
  - qmd's reranker helps paraphrase but costs temporal, because it ignores time.

## Open threads

1. **Paraphrase recall,** the main remaining gap: 0.328 against qmd-rerank's 0.475. Next step: regenerate the variants so they keep named entities, then feed them into `lcg-passages-belief-rerank`.
2. **Temporal with rerank:** 0.800 on v2 against the 0.85 target. The cross-encoder alone reaches 0.904–0.932 (E8). Consider a belief-aware first stage that is stronger on time, or ordering by belief after rerank.
3. **Router idea:** graph search wins on direct questions and passage lookups (E12). A per-question router could take some of the oracle headroom (0.814).
4. **Notes:** rerank is opt-in, and Notes needs a release, then to opt in. When it sends `queries`, its agent prompt needs the rule to keep named entities.
5. **Lexical leg and abstention (E15 → E16):** the lexical leg is any-term and unfloored, so hybrid answers 25 of 34 off-topic queries under the 0.5 floor. Probe an all-terms leg and a "BM25 must agree with the vector leg" gate (design in [`docs/research/webbrain-retrieval-suggestions.md`](https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/blob/main/docs/research/webbrain-retrieval-suggestions.md)).

# Release process

Source: https://docs.liminis.app/liminis-context-graph/release-process


This is the maintainer procedure for verifying CI status before cutting a release. It
exists because reading a job's pass/fail *conclusion* alone is not a trustworthy signal
in this repository: issue #430 found that a `2>&1 | tee <log>` pattern in six `ci.yml`
jobs (the required `test (ubuntu-latest)` gate plus all five real-corpus e2e jobs) and
three `bench.yml` steps ran under GitHub Actions' implicit default shell, which has no
`pipefail` — so each step's exit status was `tee`'s, not the piped test/bench command's.
Three consecutive `main` runs were found with `test result: FAILED` in the job log while
reporting a passing conclusion, and the masked gate let a real regression (#428) ship in
releases 0.13.0, 0.13.1, and 0.13.2, each "verified" only by reading job conclusions. See
[ADR-0430](adr/0430-ci-tee-pipefail.md) for the fix.

The fix (a workflow-level `shell: bash` default, restoring `pipefail`) makes conclusions
trustworthy going forward, but grepping the log is still the documented step here as
defense in depth: the whole point of #430 is that "the conclusion looked right" was
already true of the runs that turned out to be broken.

## Before cutting a release

For the release commit's CI run on `main`, check **both** of the following — a passing
conclusion alone is not sufficient. Set `RELEASE_SHA` to the exact commit being released
(e.g. `RELEASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`) before running either command below.

1. **Job conclusions, bound to the release commit.** `gh run list --json conclusion`
   reports the *workflow run's* overall conclusion, not each job's — and with several
   workflows (`CI`, `Release`, `Docs drift check`, ...) triggering on the same push, an
   unfiltered `--limit 1` isn't even guaranteed to return the `CI` run, nor the run for
   the specific commit being released (a later push to `main` after the release commit
   would shift `--limit 1` off it). Pin the lookup to the release commit's SHA and to a
   completed run, then check the six jobs by name — `test (ubuntu-latest)` and the five
   real-corpus e2e jobs (`real_corpus_e2e`, `mcp_real_corpus_e2e`,
   `mcp_real_corpus_mutation_e2e`, `mcp_real_corpus_admin_data_e2e`,
   `mcp_real_corpus_admin_lifecycle_e2e`) must each show `conclusion: success`:

   ```bash
   run_id=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --status completed \
     --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')
   gh run view "$run_id" --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | {name, conclusion}'
   ```

2. **Log grep for the actual test result, with retrieval failing closed.** Using that
   same `$run_id`, confirm the run's log contains no `test result: FAILED` line. Capture
   the log to a file and check `gh`'s own exit status first — piping `gh run view --log`
   straight into `grep` would make a failed log fetch (rate limit, expired log, network
   error) look identical to "no match found", which is exactly the kind of masked
   failure this document exists to avoid:

   ```bash
   gh run view "$run_id" --log > /tmp/ci-run.log   # fails loudly if retrieval fails
   grep -a "test result: FAILED" /tmp/ci-run.log
   ```

   No output from the `grep` means no failing test was masked. Any match — even
   alongside a "success" conclusion — means do not cut the release; investigate first.

Do not treat step 1 alone as sufficient evidence that "full e2e passed." Step 2 is the
one that actually verifies it.

## Response schemas are release assets

Each release carries the response JSON Schemas (`contract/*.schema.json`) and a generated
`contract-manifest.json` (`lcg_version`, `tag`, `draft`, and a sha256 per file) as release assets, beside
the binaries (#852, [ADR-0852](adr/0852-published-response-json-schemas.md)). Consumers fetch them at the
tag they pin; see the [response contract](ipc-mcp-reference.md#response-contract-json-schemas-issue-852).

- **Nothing to do by hand.** The `host` job in `release.yml` runs
  `scripts/stage-contract-assets.sh <tag> artifacts` just before `gh release create`, which attaches
  everything in `artifacts/`. The script fails the job if `contract/` holds no schemas or one is
  malformed, so a release cannot silently ship without its contract.
- **The committed schemas are already in sync.** CI's `committed_schemas_match_generated` test fails
  when `contract/*.schema.json` differ from what the source types generate, and a PR that changes a
  schema must also change `CHANGELOG.md` (`scripts/assert-contract-changelog.sh`). Before tagging,
  confirm the `[Unreleased]` changelog entries for any schema change mark breaking changes (removed or
  renamed fields, widened types, required fields made optional) as **BREAKING**, and that the section is renamed to the version being released.
- **First check after a release publishes.** `release.yml` does not run on pull requests (ADR-0639), so
  the asset step is first exercised on a tag. Confirm the release lists the seven
  `*.schema.json` files and `contract-manifest.json`, and that `jq -r .lcg_version contract-manifest.json`
  matches the tag. If it does not, fix forward; the files can be attached to the existing release with
  `scripts/stage-contract-assets.sh <tag> <dir>` followed by `gh release upload <tag> <dir>/*.json --clobber`.

## Release packaging is verified post-merge

`release.yml` does **not** run on pull requests. Release packaging — the four-target build
(`aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`,
`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), the pinned lbug extension-hash check
([ADR-0593](adr/0593-pin-lbug-extension-bytes.md)) and the OpenSSL linkage guards
([ADR-0550](adr/0550-openssl-dynamic-linkage-via-rpath.md),
[ADR-0581](adr/0581-windows-static-openssl.md)) — is verified once per merge, by the
`Release` run on the push to `main`. That run builds and checks but publishes nothing (no
GitHub Release, no announcement, no docs dispatch); only a pushed version tag publishes. See
[ADR-0639](adr/0639-post-merge-release-packaging-verification.md).

A PR that breaks packaging is therefore caught after merge and fixed forward. Before
tagging, with `RELEASE_SHA` set as above:

```bash
gh issue list --label ci-failure --label workflow:release --state open
gh run list --workflow release.yml --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --limit 5
```

A failed `Release` run on `main` files (or updates) a `ci-failure` + `workflow:release`
issue via `ci-failure-notify.yml`, and the issue closes itself on the next green run. Treat
an open one as a blocker: fix forward, or record in the release PR why the release proceeds
anyway. Failed tag-triggered runs are not reported by the listener — watch the run you just
triggered.

### Plan output lost (run red at `verify-plan`)

On a tag run, `release.yml`'s `verify-plan` job fails if the plan output reached the build jobs
empty or without a build matrix, and `host` refuses to publish unless both build jobs
succeeded ([ADR-0725](adr/0725-release-plan-output-guard.md)). The usual cause is **secret
masking**: the runner silently drops a job output that looks like a credential (for example
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` in the CHANGELOG section, which is embedded in the plan manifest).
Before this guard, that skipped the builds and published a release holding only
`dist-manifest.json` from a green run (`v0.18.0`).

If `verify-plan` is red: no release, announcement or docs dispatch happened. Find the log line
"Skip output 'val' since it may contain secret" in the `plan` job, reword the offending CHANGELOG
text, and re-cut the tag.

To verify the guard without a real release:

1. Run `scripts/test-assert-plan-output.sh` (offline; also run by CI's `lint` job).
2. End to end: on a scratch branch put credential-looking text in the CHANGELOG section for a
   throwaway pre-release version, push a tag such as `v0.0.0-guardtest.1`, and confirm
   `verify-plan` is red and `host`, `announce` and `dispatch-docs` are skipped with no release
   created. Then delete the tag. A push to `main` must still show `verify-plan` skipped and the
   builds running.

## Docs publishing

The docs site is **no longer published from `main`**. Every merge to `main` that
touches `docs/` still runs the PR-time checks below, but does not change the live
site. Publishing happens only when a release is cut, via
`.github/workflows/docs-publish.yml`. See
[ADR-0477](adr/0477-tag-based-versioned-docs-publishing.md) for the full design.

### What happens automatically when you cut a release

`release.yml` (cargo-dist) creates the GitHub Release once artifact builds finish. It
does so with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub does not start workflow runs from events created
by `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the exceptions are `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch`), so
the `release: published` event **never triggers** `docs-publish.yml` for these releases.
Instead, `release.yml`'s hand-added `dispatch-docs` job runs after the release is created
and dispatches `docs-publish.yml` with `version=<X.Y.Z>` and `ref=refs/tags/v<X.Y.Z>`
(skipping quietly for a tag that isn't `vX.Y.Z[-pre]`). The `release: published` trigger
is retained for releases created by hand (UI, or a non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` credential).
Either way, `docs-publish.yml`:

1. Skips entirely if the release's tag doesn't match the `vX.Y.Z` version-tag
   scheme (e.g. a non-version release like `eval-artifacts-2026-07`) — no docs
   action is taken.
2. Builds that tag's `docs/` tree with Jekyll, `--baseurl`-overridden to
   `/liminis-context-graph/v<version>/`, and publishes it to the `gh-pages`
   branch at that path. Every previously published version's path is left
   untouched.
3. Recomputes "latest stable release" fresh from the GitHub Releases API
   (`scripts/docs-publish-latest-stable-version.sh`) — never trusting the
   triggering event alone. If the just-published tag **is** the latest stable
   (non-prerelease) release, its build is also promoted to the site root. A
   prerelease tag only ever gets its own versioned path; it never becomes root.
4. Regenerates `gh-pages/versions.json` from what's actually on disk, which
   drives the version switcher in the page footer.

### What to check after a release publishes

1. Confirm the `Docs publish` workflow run for the release succeeded:
   `gh run list --workflow docs-publish.yml --limit 1`. For a release cut by
   `release.yml` its trigger shows as `workflow_dispatch` (dispatched by the
   `dispatch-docs` job), not `release`. If there is no such run, check the
   `dispatch-docs` job in the release workflow run: a red job means the dispatch failed
   and docs were **not** triggered (the release itself is unaffected) — publish them
   with `gh workflow run docs-publish.yml -f version=<X.Y.Z>`.
2. Visit the root URL (`https://docs.liminis.app/liminis-context-graph/`) and confirm the
   footer reads the new version.
3. Visit the new version's own URL
   (`https://docs.liminis.app/liminis-context-graph/v<version>/`) and confirm it's live.
4. Spot-check that the previous version's URL is still reachable and unchanged.

If the workflow run failed (e.g. a transient build error), re-run it with
`workflow_dispatch` rather than cutting a new release — see the republish
procedure below, which uses the exact same mechanism.

### Republishing a correction without a new release (FR-006)

Use this when the docs for an **already-released** version are wrong about
behaviour that has already shipped — the exact situation
[#473](https://github.com/verveguy/liminis-context-graph/issues/473) dealt with by
hand before this workflow existed. This procedure needs no new git tag and no new
GitHub Release.

1. Fix the docs on `main` (or a branch) as you normally would, and merge.
2. Run the publish workflow manually for the affected version:

   ```bash
   gh workflow run docs-publish.yml -f version=0.13.3
   ```

   By default this builds `refs/tags/v0.13.3` — i.e. it rebuilds the tag's own
   `docs/` tree, so it only picks up your fix if you've already fast-forwarded or
   cherry-picked it onto that tag. To publish a fix that lives on `main` instead
   (the common case), pass the ref explicitly:

   ```bash
   gh workflow run docs-publish.yml -f version=0.13.3 -f ref=main
   ```

   `docs-publish-build.sh` passes `DOCS_VERSION=0.13.3` to the site build
   regardless of which ref you build from, so the published page footer still
   reads the correct version even though the content came from `main`. (It used
   to patch `docs/_config.yml` for this; the Astro site takes the value from the
   environment instead, leaving the working tree alone.)

3. "Latest stable" is recomputed fresh from the Releases API on this run too, so
   the root URL is updated automatically if (and only if) `0.13.3` is still the
   current latest stable release. Republishing an older version never touches
   root.
4. Verify using the same steps as "What to check after a release publishes" above.

### One-time manual steps (required once, after this mechanism first ships)

Two follow-ups are manual repo-settings / one-off actions outside any PR diff
(the same category as GitHub Pages' original enablement — see ADR-0295). Until
both are done, this workflow builds and pushes to `gh-pages` correctly, but the
live site keeps serving from `main` as before:

1. **Pages source switch.** In the repository's Settings → Pages, switch
   `source.branch` from `main` to `gh-pages` (`source.path` to `/`,
   `build_type` left as `legacy`).
2. **Backfill.** Only tags carrying `site/` can be built by this workflow, since
   that is what it runs. Every tag up to and including `v0.13.3` shipped the
   Jekyll site instead and cannot be rebuilt under this scheme — the build script
   says so and exits rather than producing something misleading. Publish from the
   first release that includes the Astro site onward; there is nothing to
   backfill before it.

   Backfilling the Jekyll-era versions would mean building them with a site they
   never shipped with, which is the opposite of what per-version copies are for.

If Pages ever needs to be re-pointed (e.g. after a repository transfer), redo
step 1; the `gh-pages` branch itself is unaffected by that setting.

## Related

- [ADR-0430](adr/0430-ci-tee-pipefail.md) — the `tee`/`pipefail` defect this process
  works around, and the workflow-level fix
- [ADR-0477](adr/0477-tag-based-versioned-docs-publishing.md) — the tag-based,
  versioned docs publishing design described above
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the required gate and five e2e jobs
- `.github/workflows/docs-publish.yml` — the docs publishing workflow
- #428 — the regression that shipped behind these jobs while conclusion-only
  verification was in use
- #473 — the docs-drift audit that motivated the FR-006 republish procedure above

# Architecture Decision Records

Source: https://github.com/liminisapp/liminis-context-graph/blob/main/docs/adr/index.md


**These are historical decision records, not current-state documentation.** Each ADR captures
the reasoning behind a decision at the time it was made and is never edited to reflect later
changes — some entries below are explicitly marked `_(superseded)_`, and others (e.g. ADR-0025's
lazy index build, later revisited by ADR-0034/ADR-0036's eager build) describe behavior the
codebase has since moved past without the ADR text itself being marked. For what the system
does *today*, use the reference pages linked from the [documentation home](../) —
[Operations](../operations.md), [Configuration](../configuration.md), and
[IPC & MCP Reference](../ipc-mcp-reference.md) — and treat an ADR as the record of *why*, not a
live description of *what*.

Numbers are project-local and immutable once assigned. See [ADR-0001](0001-record-architecture-decisions.md) for the format.

**From 2026-07-30, a new ADR takes the number of the GitHub issue that motivated it** — [`0283-name-index-scan-fallback-for-endpoint-authority.md`](0283-name-index-scan-fallback-for-endpoint-authority.md), from issue #283, is the first — matching the `specs/<issue_number>-<slug>/` convention and for the same reason: a shared sequential counter is claimed at branch time, so two issues in flight always claim the same number. `0001`–`0052` predate this and keep their sequential numbers — **the gap between `0052` and the first issue-numbered ADR is expected, not missing history.** See CLAUDE.md for the full rule.

## Historical numbering

Before 2026-07, ADRs lived in two directories (`docs/adr/` numbered `0042`+ and a top-level
`adrs/` numbered from `0001`) with colliding, sometimes duplicated numbers. They were
consolidated into this directory under the single sequence above. Historical documents —
`specs/`, old issues/PRs, commit messages — may cite the old numbers; this table decodes them.
References to `ADR-035`/`ADR-042` prefixed with "the Liminis app's" refer to the parent
application's separate ADR index, not this one.

| Old (in `docs/adr/`) | New | | Old (in `adrs/`) | New |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0001 (meta) | 0001 | | 001 (wal-drain) | 0015 |
| 0042 | 0002 | | 0001 | 0012 |
| 0043 (arcswap) | 0003 | | 0002 | 0013 |
| 0043 (classify-entities) | 0004 | | 0003 | 0014 |
| 0043 (streaming-progress) | 0005 | | 0004 | 0018 |
| 0044 (embedder-http) | 0006 | | 0005 | 0019 |
| 0044 (two-hop) | 0007 | | 0006 | 0021 |
| 0045 | 0008 | | 0007 | 0022 |
| 0046 (degraded-mode) | 0009 | | 0008 | 0023 |
| 0046 (tool-use) | 0010 | | 0009 | 0024 |
| 0047 | 0011 | | 0047 | 0025 |
| 0048 | 0016 | | 0048 | 0027 |
| 0049 | 0017 | | 0049 | 0028 |
| 0050 | 0020 | | 0050 | 0029 |
| 0051 | 0026 | | 0051 | 0030 |
| | | | 0052 | 0031 |
| | | | 0053 | 0032 |
| | | | 0054 | 0033 |
